title: operational-communique-week-2026-12-08
content:
Operational Communique — week of 2026-12-06
Owner: Maya Patel (SRE lead)
Reviewed: Evan Chu, Priya Singh, Lucas Moreno
Status: in_review

Purpose
- Weekly synthesis for SRE: incidents, SLO posture, on-call handoffs, maintenance windows, and immediate action items. This is a working note — expect gaps and TODO markers.

TL;DR
- Two customer-facing incidents this week; both mitigated with fallbacks and one required a hotfix (INC-4821).
- Overall 30d request error SLI at 99.51% vs target 99.9% (error budget ~0.39% used ~0.49% over window -> we are in burn).
- Latency P95 for text-gen endpoint drifted from 180ms -> 240ms during peak on 12/07 due to a noisy batcher config; rollback applied.
- On-call handoff consolidated; new stub for multi-region failover checklist created (link above).

Incidents (short form)
1) INC-4821: Intermittent 500s on /v1/chat/stream (2026-12-07 04:12–05:06 UTC)
   - Symptom: clients saw 500s and truncated streams for ~54 minutes. Error spike correlated with batched-config change rolled at 03:58 UTC.
   - Root cause (prelim): batching aggregator introduced a pathological queue-hold when certain token distributions hit a slow kernel path; queue starvation cascaded to worker OOMs.
   - Mitigation: Reverted batching-config to prior safe profile at 04:24 UTC. Autoscaler promoted standby nodes; traffic routed to fallback smaller-batch variant for 30m. Hotfix PR merged to add a defensive queue timeout (PR #2345).
   - Impact: ~2.2% requests experienced 500s during spike window; regen attempts recovered ~70% of user requests.
   - Follow-ups: Add a load-test that simulates the token distribution; change deploy gating to include a short smoke test on trace path. Owner: Evan (due 2026-12-15).

2) OPS-1198: Metrics ingestion lag (2026-12-06 13:00–15:40 UTC)
   - Symptom: aggregated SLO pipelines delayed, alerting delayed by ~1.5h.
   - Root cause: Cassandra compaction coinciding with backup snapshot; ingestion worker backpressure.
   - Mitigation: Throttled compaction ops and spun an ephemeral metrics-insert worker to catch up.
   - Follow-ups: Revisit snapshot timing; add circuit-breaker to ingestion worker. Owner: Priya (due 2026-12-13).

SLO / Error budget snapshot (30d window ending 2026-12-08)
- Availability SLO (API success rate): target 99.9%
  - Current: 99.51%
  - Error budget burn: 0.49% (exceeds target by 0.09% over window)
- Latency SLO (P95 text-gen <= 220ms): target met 86% of time
  - Current P95: 210ms average, but spike to 240ms on 12/07
- Observations: primary risk is variability during small-burst peaks caused by batching policy changes. We should prioritize conservative ship gating for batch-related PRs.

On-call handoff notes (for incoming shift)
- Handoff time: 2026-12-09 07:00 UTC
- Receivers: Lucas Moreno (night shift)
- Outstanding items to monitor:
  1) INC-4821 follow-up (Evan) — confirm hotfix stabilizes under canary traffic.
  2) OPS-1198 ingestion health — metrics backlog catch-up scheduled overnight.
  3) Canary rollout queue: we have one active canary for batcher-hotfix on "canary-east-02" (5% traffic). Monitor p95 and error spike.
  4) Scheduled maintenance: GPU firmware update in eu-west-1 on 2026-12-10 02:00–03:00 UTC. Expected window: transient 100–200ms tail latency for affected vessels.
- Escalation policy reminders: Pager -> Primary on-call -> SRE lead (Maya) after 15m unresolved P1.
- Runbook pointers: see Confluence: SRE-RUNBOOK-V2 -> sections: "streaming-recovery", "batcher-tuning". Not all steps updated after last month — flagged below.

Operational observations / notes to self
- Deploy practices: We are still allowing extended batching-config changes to land without a focused load-profile test. Proposal: require a fast synthetic test that hits the kernel path (script in infra/tools) as part of the deployment pipeline for batcher-related PRs.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool "dedicated-us-1" sustained 92% GPU memory utilization during peak; consider pre-warming an extra standby when predictably close to 90% for >30m. Owner: infra-capacity team (request submitted).
- Alerts tuning: Several alerts thresholded at absolute counts (e.g., "error-rate > 50/min"). Need to switch to rate-per-100k or pct-based thresholds to avoid noisy pages during traffic surges.

Action items (concise)
- Evan: Create synthetic load test for token-distribution edge-case and add to ci-smoke (due 2026-12-15).
- Priya: Implement ingestion circuit-breaker and reschedule snapshotting (due 2026-12-13).
- Lucas: Nightly check on canary-east-02 during first 3 hours of shift; escalate any p95 deltas beyond +20% (ongoing).
- Maya: Draft deploy gating checklist for batching config changes (first draft due 2026-12-12).
- Infra team: Evaluate standby pre-warm policy for dedicated-us-1 (request id: CAP-2026-83).

Runbook / docs gaps (quick list)
- streaming-recovery runbook needs explicit section for "queue-timeout" fallback and how to force drain a stalled aggregator.
- batcher-tuning doc lacks concrete guidance for kernel-path detection; add steps to collect kernel traces + telemetry markers.
- maintenance-runbook: add checklist item to notify CS for potentially impacted long-running customer exports.

Meetings / syncs scheduled
- Post-incident retro (INC-4821): 2026-12-10 16:00 UTC (30m) — required: Evan, Maya, infra eng, product owner for chat routes.
- SLO review / prioritization: 2026-12-14 10:00 UTC — review 30d burn, decide on emergency throttles if burn continues.
- Runbook working session: 2026-12-11 09:00 UTC — focus on streaming-recovery updates.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we auto-fallback to smaller-batch variants on any batcher reconfiguration? (operational cost vs risk). Dev/Prod tradeoff — need product input.
- What is acceptable overnight burn before triggers for emergency throttles? Standard cadence says 3-day smoothing; consider probability-weighted approach.

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (topline numbers)
- 30d total requests: 1.8B
- 30d failed requests: 8.1M (~0.45%)
- Spike peak RPS (12/07 04:00 UTC): 18.2k RPS
- Average P95 text-gen (rolling 7d): 199ms

Notes to reader
- This doc is a working comms artifact intended for SRE and cross-functional partners. Add comments inline or push edits to the canary-hotfix PR for quick traceability.
- If you pick up an action, please add yourself to the collaborators list and update status.

-- Maya
